memory_update.text: MKSI should be promoted as the clearest US-listed underfollowed candidate for the ABF / high-end substrate node because Atotech maps directly to plating equipment and proprietary chemistry for PCB/substrate manufacturers.

The purest ABF and high-end substrate assets appear mostly non-US listed: Ajinomoto, Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron, Nan Ya PCB, and AT&S. US-listed exposure likely requires second-order mapping through equipment, chemistry, inspection, or packaging tools.
For later layers, separate three subnodes: ABF/build-up film materials, high-end IC substrate capacity, and process enablers such as plating chemistry/equipment and inspection/metrology.

CAMT and KLIC are plausible but unverified US-listed second-order candidates; they should not survive Layer 2 unless filings or transcripts confirm advanced packaging, substrate, HBM, chiplet, or AI-server package exposure.

summary: This Layer 1B pass expands the US-listed universe around the ABF / high-end IC substrate bottleneck. The clearest US-listed underfollowed candidate from provided evidence is MKS Inc., via Atotech plating equipment and proprietary chemistry sold into PCB/substrate manufacturers. Because the core substrate makers and ABF supplier are mostly non-US listed, the US-listed discovery lane tilts toward second-order equipment, chemistry, inspection/metrology, and packaging-tool suppliers rather than pure substrate capacity owners. TSM is retained only as a reference anchor; the main alpha-hunt lane is MKSI, CAMT, and KLIC, with CAMT/KLIC explicitly requiring evidence verification.
